To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we propose a novel approach to Bayesian Causal Discovery (BCD), (ii) we show that our BCD Nets are able to learn DAGs from data, (iii) we show that BCD Nets are more scalable than state-of-the-art methods, (iv) we show that the learned DAGs are of better quality than state-of-the-arts.

(1) the proposed BCD nets approach is able to learn a causal structure from data, (2) the learned causal model is able to predict the effect of interventions, and (3) the learned model is able to identify the causal effect of interventions in the presence of confounding variables

(1) The BCD net approach is a scalable method to learn DAGs from data, (2) the method is able to learn causal relationships from data with a small number of samples, (3) the method is robust with respect to noise, and (4) the method scales well to large datasets
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods to learn the structure of a DAG from data and with the development of algorithms to efficiently compute causal quantities from the learned DAGs.
the problem of learning causal models from observational data, which we call the causal learning problem.
developing scalable and robust methods for Bayesian inference in causal models, and applying them to real data sets.

the SEM framework is a good choice to model causal relationships in a DAG, and the BCD Nets approach is a good choice for estimating the causal relationships in a SEM.
the BCD algorithm is a good choice for causal discovery in small and medium-sized data sets.
the BCD nets are a promising approach to the problem of causal discovery.
